Delhi Weather: Red Alert Issued For THESE Parts Of The City; Will Moon Sighting Be Affected?
The moonrise time in Delhi on October 29 is around 8:11 pm to 8:17 pm. Everyone is hoping that the moon appears on time so that women observing the fast can carry on with their rituals.
Delhiites, especially women keeping the Karwa Chauth fast, may face trouble with the moon sighting in Delhi-NCR due to the weather today. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for several parts of Delhi, which means rain along with intense thunderstorms is expected during the evening hours. Here’s what you should know.
Delhi Weather Turns Cloudy
According to Hindustan Times, the IMD has issued red and orange alerts for moderate to heavy rain in parts of Delhi on October 29, 2026. Cloudy skies are expected on Karwa Chauth, which means the moon sighting could be affected. A red alert is in place for North Delhi, North West Delhi and South West Delhi. Meanwhile, an orange alert is in place for Central Delhi, North East Delhi and South East Delhi.
These alerts mean there is a possibility of moderate thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and hail in parts of Delhi. Some areas could also witness thunderstorms with moderate rainfall. Women keeping the Karwa Chauth fast may have to wait a little longer for the moon to appear before breaking their fast.
According to Hindustan Times, the moonrise time in Delhi on October 29 is around 8:11 pm to 8:17 pm. Everyone is hoping that the moon appears on time so that women observing the fast can carry on with their rituals. Thunderstorms and rain are also likely in the capital on October 30. The minimum temperature is expected to be 17°C and the maximum will reach 27°C.
The weather is expected to change again on November 1, when clear skies will replace cloudy skies until November 4. Delhi residents are already feeling the chill in the air as they gear up to officially welcome the winter season in the city. Uttarakhand, on the other hand, is witnessing snowfall for the second time within a week. Visuals on social media are going viral, showing Kedarnath Temple covered in white while devotees queue up outside for darshan.
